summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause: there are no confirmed US or Israeli strikes on Iran in recent weeks, but Iran is still attacking ships around the Strait of Hormuz, the US blockade of Iranian ports continues, and talks on a new draft deal are under way. Hormuz is open only in part, with oil flows well below normal.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are open under US control. Most ships now pass through a US-run transit system (101 transits over Oct 22–24, against about 138 a day in 2025), with only a handful a day outside it.

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: Around 11.6 to 11.7 million barrels a day in October, against about 17.1 million before the war (Kpler).

status.label: The war
status.note: No confirmed US or Israeli strikes on Iran in recent weeks (AFP reported none on Iranian targets since early September). Trump said on Oct 8 the US would not resume strikes before the Nov 3 midterms; reports say renewed strikes are being prepared for after that.

status.label: Brent crude
status.value: US$111.92 (January contract, early Monday trade in Asia)
status.note: Brent was at US$111.92, down US$1.51 (1.3%), and WTI at US$102.34, down US$1.78, at 23:03 GMT on Nov 1 as Iran-Qatar talks continued (Reuters). Brent for January settled at US$113.43 on Friday Oct 30.

updates.text: Oil fell in early Asian trade on Monday as Iranian and Qatari officials held a third straight day of talks: Brent was at US$111.92, down 1.3%, and WTI at US$102.34 at 23:03 GMT.

Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday evening that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days, down from seven, and that Iran does not plan direct meetings with US officials; Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei told commanders to prepare for possible new US-Israeli strikes.
Qatar's state news agency said the LNG carrier Al Mayeda was struck by 'unidentified objects' in Gulf waters on Friday evening; no crew were injured and the ship remained operational.

Iranian state media aired footage on Nov 1 of missiles and drones being moved out of underground storage, and Iran's general staff, the IRGC and the army said they were ready to launch missile and drone attacks if fighting resumes.

Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei told military commanders that any threat must be met with an 'immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response' and ordered an updated list of US and Israeli targets (IRNA).
President Trump said peace talks with Iran were going 'fine' but questioned whether Iran's negotiators could be trusted, and said the US could hit Iran's remaining nuclear sites 'in ten minutes'.
Iran's deputy parliament speaker Ali Nikzad said the window for talks had closed and warned of an 'immediate, effective response without geographical limits' to any renewed confrontation.
President Trump said negotiations with Iran were 'going fine' but that he was 'not in that much of a hurry' to reach a deal.

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
